question: How much does knowledge of enemy Flag/Spy, or all enemy ranks, improve Context Teacher against DOS?
idea: Flag/Spy knowledge removes uncertainty about the objective and Spy risk. Exact-rank knowledge additionally removes uncertainty about battles. Compare with unchanged masked teacher to locate information-related weakness.
comparison: All three policies use identical armies and seeds within each cohort; swapped sides in every pair. No tuning after pilot. Run fresh validation with the same frozen policies.
analysis: Report all scored wins/draws/losses and unscored errors. Stratified paired bootstrap with 10000 resamples, analysis seed 1940002: each score on complete scored pairs; matched differences on pairs fully scored in both arms. Report pilot and validation separately. Positive validation difference interval establishes improvement for this diagnostic, not suitability for production.
limits: DOS has initial Flag/Spy knowledge plus conditional access to other true ranks. Flag/Spy arm isolates initial identities, not the full DOS knowledge schedule. All-rank arm is a broader intervention. Our simulated opponent still has masked knowledge of our ranks. Privileged enemy ranks are represented with the existing revealed bit, so this also changes known-piece heuristics. No production change or fairness claim.
privacy: Only named diagnostic policies receive opponent-setup in addition to original DOS policies. Ordinary policy IDs and frozen sources remain unchanged.
settings: Both diagnostics retain eight samples, depth four, correction blend, strategic utility and root context. In the all-rank arm all eight worlds coincide; the simulated opponent does not become the actual DOS policy.
